roadmap.subtitle: 4-page rapid mastery of Git core mental models, branching, and collaboration
how_to_use: Page 3 sets the **3-stage architecture** — master Working Tree, Index & Repo before memorising commands.
Page 4 covers **branching, pointers & merging** — how `switch` & `restore` cleanly replace legacy `checkout`.
Page 5 covers **syncing with remotes** — the mechanics of `fetch`, `pull`, `push`, and resolving merge conflicts.
Page 6 is your **cheat sheet & interview guide** — 12 mini-guides, 10 questions, and the ultimate Git formula.
Do the sample commands yourself in a sandbox directory to build muscle memory.
mindset: Git does not store diffs; it stores full **snapshots** of your project on every commit.
Commits form a **Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)** where each node points back to parent commits.
Nearly every operation is **local-first**; network latency only matters during `fetch`, `pull`, and `push`.
Git rarely deletes data. If you lose work, `git reflog` can usually rescue orphaned commits.
tools: **Git CLI:** Version 2.23+ recommended to use `switch` & `restore` syntax.
**Terminal Shell:** zsh or bash with Git branch auto-completion enabled.
**Hosting Platform:** GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket for remote collaboration.
**Visual DAG Viewers:** Built-in `git log --graph --oneline` or VS Code Git Graph extension.
**Productivity Aliases:** Setup `git config --global alias.st status` and `alias.co checkout`.
note: **Default Branch:** Now `main` instead of `master` (`git config --global init.defaultBranch main`).
**Replaced checkout:** Modern Git uses `git switch` (branch navigation) and `git restore` (undoing changes).
**Atomic Commits:** Make small, focused commits with imperative messages (e.g. `feat: add user auth`).
**Never Rebase Public Branches:** Only rebase local unpublished branches to avoid rewriting shared history.

pages.title: The Three Trees: Work, Stage & Commit
pages.subtitle: Understanding how Git moves changes through working directory, index, and repository

ul: **Distributed VCS:** Every developer clone holds the entire project history and complete object graph locally on disk.
**Snapshot Model:** Unlike legacy VCS tracking diff deltas, Git captures immutable **snapshots** of the directory tree.
**Cryptographic Integrity:** Every object is content-addressed by a 40-character SHA hash, preventing silent corruption.
**Working Directory:** Local sandbox files you edit directly in your code editor.
**Staging Area (Index):** Binary cache (`.git/index`) preparing the exact snapshot for commit.
**Repository (.git):** Permanent object database storing verified snapshots & history graph.
**Blob:** Compressed raw file content (stores zero filenames or permissions).
**Tree:** Represents a directory; maps filenames & modes to child blob/tree SHAs.
**Commit:** Points to root tree SHA, parent commit(s), author, timestamp, and message.
**Annotated Tag:** Permanent named reference pointing directly to a specific commit.

ul: Editing files and forgetting to stage. Fix: Check `git status` before running commit.
Committing secrets, .env, or node_modules. Fix: Add patterns to `.gitignore` before initial add.
Vague commit messages like 'fixed stuff'. Fix: Write clear imperative summaries like `feat: add user login`.
Accidentally staged the wrong file. Fix: Run `git restore --staged <file>` to unstage without losing edits.

blocks.remember: Edit in Working Tree, Buffer in Staging Index, Save permanently in Repository Snapshot.

footer.text: Atomic commits allow easy rollbacks, clear code reviews, and clean bisecting when bugs arise.
Q: What is the Staging Area? A: An intermediate buffer allowing selective, atomic commits.
Use `git add -p` (patch mode) to review and stage specific chunks of code interactively.

pages.title: Branching, Merging & Moving HEAD
pages.subtitle: How Git tracks divergent lines of development with lightweight movable pointers

ul: **Pointer Model:** A branch is simply a lightweight 41-byte text file storing a 40-hex commit hash (`.git/refs/heads/<name>`).
**Zero Overhead:** Creating or switching branches is instant; zero files are duplicated.
**HEAD Cursor:** References whichever branch or commit is currently checked out (`.git/HEAD`).
**Auto-Advance:** When you commit, Git automatically advances the current branch pointer.

head: Strategy
Behavior
History Impact
rows: Replays commits on top of base

blocks.code:
# 1. Create and isolate feature branch
git switch -c feature/auth-token
# ... edit files and commit ...
git commit -am "feat: add login token validation"
# 2. Switch back and integrate into main
git switch main
git merge --no-ff feature/auth-token
blocks.label: Branch & Merge Workflow

blocks.out:
Merge made by the 'ort' strategy.
 auth.py | 24 +++++++++++++++++++++---
 1 file changed, 21 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)
blocks.label: 3-way merge output

ul: **`git stash -u`:** Shelves dirty changes (including untracked files).
**`git stash pop`:** Re-applies the most recent stash and deletes it.
**`git stash list`:** Inspects all saved stash entries across branches.
**`git stash drop`:** Permanently discards a specific saved stash state.
Detached HEAD state. Fix: Run `git switch main`.
Rebasing shared branches. Fix: Never rebase commits pushed to remote.
Branch switch blocked. Fix: Run `git stash`, switch, then `git stash pop`.
Wrong branch commit. Fix: `git cherry-pick <hash>` on target, then reset.

blocks.remember: Branches are 41-byte pointers; HEAD is where you stand. Switch cleanly with git switch.

footer.text: Feature branches isolate experimental code without touching stable production main.
Q: Git Merge vs Rebase? A: Merge preserves historical context; rebase rewrites linear history.
Run `git log --oneline --graph --all` to view your branch topology in the terminal.

pages.title: Remotes, Syncing & Resolving Conflicts
pages.subtitle: Connecting to remote repositories, sharing commits, and resolving merge conflicts

ul: **Remote Server:** A repository hosted on a network or cloud platform (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket).
**Origin Convention:** Git automatically names the default upstream remote **`origin`** (`.git/config`).
**Tracking Branches:** References like `origin/main` are read-only local caches of remote state.
**Offline-First:** All commit and diff operations occur offline; network sync is explicit.
**Divergent Edits:** Occurs when two branches edit the exact same lines, or one deletes an edited file.
**Automatic Pause:** Git halts the merge and injects markers into affected files in the workdir.
**Resolution Flow:** Choose desired lines, remove markers, stage with `git add`, and finalize with `commit`.

blocks.code:
# 1. Inside conflicted settings.py:
<<<<<<< HEAD
DATABASE_PORT = 5432  # Production port
=======
DATABASE_PORT = 5433  # Staging update
>>>>>>> feature/port-update

# 2. Pick desired line, delete markers, then:
git add settings.py
git commit -m "fix: resolve database port conflict"
blocks.label: Conflict markers & resolution

blocks.out:
[main 9a2b1c4] fix: resolve database port conflict
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)
blocks.label: Resolution commit output

ul: **Set Upstream Tracking:** Use `git push -u origin <branch>` once.
**Rebase Before Push:** `git pull --rebase` avoids messy merge bubbles.
**Small Focused PRs:** Keep PRs under 300 lines for fast review.
**Protected Branches:** Mandate peer reviews and CI checks on `main`.
Push rejected (non-fast-forward). Fix: Run `git pull --rebase`, then push.
Raw `git push --force` on main. Fix: Use `--force-with-lease`.
Panic on conflict markers. Fix: Run `git merge --abort`.
Pushed to wrong remote branch. Fix: Set `push.default simple`.

blocks.remember: Fetch is safe inspection; Pull is fetch plus merge. Resolve markers, stage, and commit to settle conflicts.

footer.text: Continuous Integration (CI) systems trigger builds and test suites on git push events.
Q: git fetch vs git pull? A: Fetch downloads objects without modifying working files; pull merges them.
Configure `git config --global pull.rebase true` to keep pull histories clean and linear.

pages.title: Git Basics Cheat Sheet & Interview Guide
pages.subtitle: 12 key concepts, 10 must-know interview questions, and the ultimate Git formula

ul: Stores full trees, never diff deltas.
Log of every `HEAD` move on disk.

ol: **What is the difference between Git and SVN?** Git is distributed with full local snapshots; SVN is centralised and diff-based.
**What happens internally when you commit?** Git writes blob objects for files, a tree object for directories, and a commit object with metadata.
**What is the staging area (index) and why does it exist?** It provides an intermediate buffer allowing developers to craft atomic, granular commits.
**Explain git fetch vs git pull.** Fetch updates remote-tracking references without touching working files; pull fetches and immediately merges.
**How does Fast-Forward merge differ from 3-Way merge?** Fast-forward moves the branch label forward linearly; 3-way creates a merge commit from a common ancestor.
**What is git rebase and when is it dangerous?** It replays commits on top of another base to linearize history. Dangerous if run on shared public branches.
**What is a detached HEAD state?** HEAD points directly to a commit hash rather than a named branch; new commits risk being orphaned.
**How do you resolve a merge conflict?** Open the conflicted file, manually choose desired lines, delete `<<<<<<<` and `>>>>>>>` markers, stage, and commit.
**Difference between git reset, git revert, and git restore?** Reset rewrites branch pointer; revert creates an inverse commit; restore affects working tree / index.
**How can you recover a commit lost to git reset --hard?** Run `git reflog` to identify the orphaned commit hash, then `git switch -c recovery <hash>`.

blocks.remember: Snapshot -> Stage -> Commit -> Branch -> Fetch -> Merge (Recover with Reflog)

footer.text: Daily reference sheet for code reviews, onboarding engineers, and resolving git blocks.
Mastering the DAG mental model answers 90% of all Git technical interview questions.
When stuck, run git status and git reflog before running destructive commands.

verification.fact: Git switch and restore introduced in Git 2.23 (August 2019)
Default initial branch name changed from master to main in modern Git
SHA-1 hashing transition to SHA-256 (Object Format)
Git merge default strategy in modern Git is 'ort' (replaces recursive)
